accepted.reason: Best observation-target alignment: hospitalization admissions plausibly lag infections, and a fixed 1-week delayed_I is a parsimonious way to correct peak timing without introducing an explicit H compartment that may be weakly identifiable in a 31-week single-season series. Avoids fractional-memory overfitting risk while addressing the main semantic mismatch of obs=I.

Identifiable baseline comparator with minimal degrees of freedom; useful as a no-lag reference. However, obs=I is not well aligned to hospitalization-rate semantics and may systematically lead the peak, especially in a high-peakiness series.

Still within a simple SEIR + delayed_I family and respects hospitalization lag semantics, but a 2-week fixed delay is more likely to over-shift peaks and force compensatory latent-dynamics distortion in short single-season data; higher risk of weak identifiability of the delay parameter.

rejected.reason: SEIRS adds a waning-immunity parameter that is typically weakly identifiable in a single-season window and can mimic other effects (time-varying transmission, reporting changes), increasing over-complexity risk without improving hospitalization-target alignment (still obs=I, no delay).

Fractional memory is not clearly justified by the provided series summary (single season, high peakiness but no indication of long-memory behavior). Fractional SEIR increases identifiability risk and can overfit by absorbing timing/shape errors that are more plausibly explained by an observation lag (delayed_I) for hospitalization-rate targets.

suggested_edits.edit: If kept, consider switching observation_map from I to delayed_I with delay_weeks=1 to better align with hospitalization-rate semantics while retaining baseline simplicity.

Constrain interpretation as a sensitivity check only (0–2 week lag), and be cautious about allowing other flexible components simultaneously; if instability appears, prefer delay_weeks=1 over 2 for identifiability in a 31-week season.

If the goal is sharper peaks, prefer addressing observation-target mismatch first (delayed_I) rather than adding waning; otherwise, restrict waning to be effectively negligible over one season to reduce identifiability issues.

If fractional dynamics are explored, pair with delayed_I rather than obs=I only if strictly necessary, and treat as a low-priority robustness probe due to overfitting/identifiability risk in short single-season data.
